questions.stem: PROJECT TIGER was launched in INDIA in:
questions.explanation: PROJECT TIGER — launched 1 APRIL 1973 by PM INDIRA GANDHI's government. INITIAL: 9 tiger reserves covering ~14,000 sq km — Corbett (Uttarakhand), Manas (Assam), Palamau (Jharkhand), Simlipal (Odisha), Bandipur (Karnataka), Melghat (Maharashtra), Kanha (MP), Ranthambore (Rajasthan), Sundarbans (WB). MOTIVATION: by 1972, Bengal tiger population had declined to ~1,800 from ~40,000 in 1900 — alarming poaching + habitat loss. NOW: 56 TIGER RESERVES (2024) covering ~78,000 sq km (~2.4% of India's land area). NATIONAL TIGER CONSERVATION AUTHORITY (NTCA, 2006) — statutory body under Wildlife Protection Act 1972 (amended 2006) to oversee Project Tiger. TIGER CENSUS by NTCA (every 4 years): (1) 2006: 1,411 tigers. (2) 2010: 1,706. (3) 2014: 2,226. (4) 2018: 2,967. (5) 2022: 3,167 (~71% of world's wild tigers). India hosts the WORLD'S LARGEST tiger population. FUNDING: ~₹400 crore/year central + state contribution. CONSERVATION SUCCESS: tiger population MORE THAN DOUBLED in 16 years (2006-2022). CHALLENGES: human-wildlife conflict, dispersal corridors, poaching pressure (still occurs). RECENT: 50 YEARS OF PROJECT TIGER celebration (April 2023, Mysuru) — PM Modi launched 'INTERNATIONAL BIG CATS ALLIANCE'. PYQ FREQUENCY: Project Tiger basics in UPSC, SSC, NDA — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: BANDHAVGARH National Park, famous for high tiger density, is in which state?
questions.explanation: BANDHAVGARH NATIONAL PARK — UMARIA district, MADHYA PRADESH. Area: ~448 sq km core + ~820 sq km buffer = ~1,536 sq km tiger reserve. ESTABLISHED: 1968 NP, 1993 tiger reserve. TIGER DENSITY: among the HIGHEST in India — ~135 tigers as of 2022; ~7-8 tigers per 100 sq km. RAJOR ATTRACTIONS: BANDHAVGARH FORT — 2,000-year-old hilltop fort (cited in Ramayana — Lakshmana built it for his brother Bharata; 'Bandhav-garh' = brother's fort); HUNDREDS of CAVES from 1st century BCE-CE, with rock paintings; SHESHSHAYYA — sculpture of Vishnu reclining on serpent. WHITE TIGERS: discovered in WILD here — MOHAN (1951), captured by Maharaja Martand Singh of Rewa, became basis of all white tigers in zoos. Now no wild whites; in zoos only. MADHYA PRADESH — known as 'TIGER STATE OF INDIA'; hosts SIX tiger reserves: (1) BANDHAVGARH. (2) KANHA — inspiration for Kipling's 'Jungle Book' (Sher Khan's territory; Mowgli area). (3) PENCH — also Jungle Book setting. (4) SATPURA — central highlands. (5) PANNA — back from extinction (zero tigers in 2009; ~80 by 2022). (6) SANJAY-DUBRI. Plus RANTHAMBORE (Rajasthan) — for comparison. PYQ FREQUENCY: Bandhavgarh-MP in SSC GA, UPSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Per the 2022 Tiger Census, INDIA had approximately HOW MANY wild tigers?
questions.explanation: INDIA TIGER POPULATION (2022 census, results announced 9 April 2023): 3,167 tigers — approximately 71% of WORLD'S wild tiger population. World total: ~4,500-5,000. METHODOLOGY: M-STrIPES (Monitoring System for Tigers — Intensive Protection and Ecological Status) — combines camera traps, scat-DNA, footprint analysis, satellite imagery. Each tiger photographed by trap cameras has UNIQUE STRIPE PATTERN (like fingerprints) — counted individually. STATE-WISE: Madhya Pradesh ~785 (highest); Karnataka ~563 (2nd); Uttarakhand ~560 (3rd); Maharashtra ~444; Tamil Nadu ~306; Kerala ~213; Assam ~190. RECENT NEW RESERVES: Veerangana Durgavati (MP, 2023), Madhav Tiger Reserve (MP, 2025) — taking total to 56. WORLD TIGER DAY: 29 JULY (since 2010, St. Petersburg Tiger Summit, where 13 'tiger range' countries pledged to DOUBLE tigers by 2022 — TX2 GOAL — India achieved this 4 years early). 'TIGER RANGE COUNTRIES': India, Russia, China, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia (extinct). KEY THREATS: poaching for skin/bones (Chinese traditional medicine), habitat fragmentation, human-wildlife conflict. SUCCESS PILLARS: protected areas + community-based conservation + cross-border cooperation. PYQ FREQUENCY: tiger census + WORLD share in UPSC, SSC GA — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: NAGARHOLE NATIONAL PARK / Tiger Reserve is located in:
questions.explanation: NAGARHOLE NATIONAL PARK — KARNATAKA, in KODAGU (Coorg) + MYSURU districts. Area: ~847 sq km. Original name: RAJIV GANDHI NATIONAL PARK (renamed for the former PM in 1992). NAME 'NAGARHOLE' = 'snake river' in Kannada (Naga + Hole = serpentine river that flows through the park). PART OF NILGIRI BIOSPHERE RESERVE — UNESCO heritage cluster: Nagarhole + Bandipur (Karnataka) + Wayanad (Kerala) + Mudumalai (Tamil Nadu) + Mukurthi (TN). Forms a CONTIGUOUS LANDSCAPE crucial for tiger + elephant connectivity. TIGERS at Nagarhole: ~150+ (one of highest densities in India). Other species: Asian elephant (~3,000+ in greater Nilgiri block, world's largest population), gaur, sambar, leopard, dhole (Indian wild dog), sloth bear. KABINI RESERVOIR within the park — winter dry season concentrates wildlife near water; great for safari. NATIVE COMMUNITIES: JENU KURUBA, BETTA KURUBA tribes traditionally lived here; relocated mostly outside park (some controversy over rehabilitation policies). PROJECT TIGER reserve since 1999. KARNATAKA tiger reserves: (1) Nagarhole. (2) Bandipur. (3) Bhadra. (4) Anshi-Dandeli. (5) BRT (Biligiri Ranganatha Temple). PYQ FREQUENCY: state-tiger reserve mapping in SSC GA, UPSC, KAS — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which Indian tiger reserve is FAMOUS for its TIGERS THAT SWIM in saline waters and HUNT in mangroves?
questions.explanation: SUNDARBANS TIGER RESERVE — UNIQUE among tiger habitats; the WORLD'S LARGEST mangrove forest, in WEST BENGAL (and continuing into Bangladesh). Area: ~2,585 sq km tiger reserve in Indian portion; ~10,000 sq km total ecosystem. UNESCO World Heritage 1987; Ramsar wetland; Biosphere Reserve. UNIQUE TIGER ADAPTATIONS: (1) SWIM regularly in tidal channels and saline water — only place in world where tigers swim daily (other tigers can swim but Sundarbans tigers do it as routine). (2) Hunt aquatic prey — fish, crabs, monitor lizards, deer crossing channels. (3) Drink BRACKISH water (low salinity tolerance). (4) Sometimes attack humans entering forest for honey, fish, wood — Sundarbans is the WORLD'S MOST DANGEROUS TIGER REGION for humans (~30-50 deaths/year historically; declining with awareness + protection). TIGER COUNT (2022): ~96 in Indian Sundarbans. CHALLENGES: (1) RISING SEA LEVELS — climate change threatens habitat. (2) CYCLONES — Aila 2009, Amphan 2020 devastated. (3) PROXIMITY TO HUMAN VILLAGES — conflict. CYCLONES + storm surges have submerged some islands (Lohachara, Bedford). NEIGHBORING fauna: estuarine crocodile, water monitor, Olive Ridley turtle, Gangetic dolphin (rare). HEAD MASKS worn by villagers (mask of human face on back of head — tigers attack from behind, mask deceives them) — partial success. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sundarbans-tiger uniqueness in UPSC, SSC, NDA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: SARISKA Tiger Reserve, which famously had ZERO tigers in 2005, is in:
questions.explanation: SARISKA TIGER RESERVE — ALWAR district, RAJASTHAN (Aravalli hills). Area: 881 sq km; Project Tiger reserve since 1978. INFAMOUS FOR: 'TIGER WIPE-OUT' — by 2005, ALL tigers had been POACHED (last sighting 2003); officially confirmed ZERO tigers in 2005 — major embarrassment for Project Tiger; sparked policy reforms + creation of NTCA (2006). REINTRODUCTION (2008): tigers from Ranthambore translocated by helicopter — first ever such reintroduction in India. Slow recovery — ~25-30 tigers as of 2024. PROBLEMS faced: (1) POACHING gangs (organized crime, some allegedly with insider help). (2) HUMAN VILLAGES inside — ~25 villages (~5,000 people) still inside reserve; cattle grazing competes with prey species. (3) SARISKA HIGHWAY: NH-248A — passes through critical tiger habitat; nighttime traffic disrupts wildlife. KEY SITE: KANKWARI FORT (16th c.) — Aurangzeb imprisoned brother Dara Shikoh here; popular tourist spot WITHIN reserve. NEAR ATTRACTIONS: PANDUPOL HANUMAN TEMPLE (Mahabharata legend); Bhangarh Fort (haunted reputation). RECENT — VILLAGE RELOCATION: gradual (slow) relocation of villages; ~5 done; 20 remain. PROJECT TIGER REVIEW: Sariska episode triggered TIGER TASK FORCE (2005, headed by Sunita Narain) → recommendations led to: (1) NTCA establishment (2006). (2) M-STrIPES protocol for monitoring. (3) Larger buffer zones. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sariska story in UPSC, SSC.

questions.stem: WORLD TIGER DAY is observed annually on:
questions.explanation: WORLD TIGER DAY — 29 JULY annually. ORIGIN: 2010 ST. PETERSBURG TIGER SUMMIT in Russia, where 13 TIGER RANGE COUNTRIES pledged to DOUBLE wild tiger population by 2022 (TX2 goal). India achieved this milestone EARLY (by 2018); other countries had mixed results. 13 TIGER RANGE COUNTRIES: India, Russia, China, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia. As of 2022 STATUS: India ~3,167 (largest); Russia ~600 (Amur tigers in Far East); Indonesia ~400 (Sumatran). EXTINCT in: Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos (functionally), Singapore (long ago), Bali, Java. KEY GLOBAL OBSERVANCES related to wildlife: (1) WORLD WILDLIFE DAY — 3 March. (2) WORLD ENVIRONMENT DAY — 5 June (PM Modi's 'Mission LiFE' launched on this day 2022). (3) WORLD TIGER DAY — 29 July. (4) WORLD ELEPHANT DAY — 12 August. (5) WORLD LION DAY — 10 August. (6) WORLD MIGRATORY BIRD DAY — 2nd Sat of May + Oct. INDIA-SPECIFIC: (a) PROJECT TIGER ANNIVERSARY — 1 April (1973). (b) PROJECT ELEPHANT — 1992. (c) PROJECT LION — 2018 (for Asiatic lions). PROJECT CHEETAH — 2022 (reintroduction at Kuno NP). NATIONAL ANIMAL: Bengal Tiger (since 1972, replaced lion which was prior). PYQ FREQUENCY: World Tiger Day in SSC GA, UPSC current affairs 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which was the first Tiger Reserve established under Project Tiger (1973) in India?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett (Uttarakhand) was the first of the nine reserves launched under Project Tiger in 1973.

questions.stem: Project Tiger was launched in India in which year?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 with 9 reserves; now has 55+ reserves.

questions.stem: Which state has the highest number of tiger reserves in India?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh hosts the most tiger reserves (Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Panna, Satpura, Sanjay-Dubri) and is called the 'Tiger State'.

questions.stem: The Sundarbans Tiger Reserve spans parts of West Bengal and which other country?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans mangrove forest is shared between India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.stem: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve is the largest tiger reserve by area in India. In which state is it?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (ca. 3,728 sq km) spans Telangana and AP; it straddles the Krishna River.

questions.stem: Bandipur Tiger Reserve in Karnataka is adjacent to which other tiger reserve across the state border?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Bandipur (Karnataka), Mudumalai (Tamil Nadu), Wayanad (Kerala) and Nagarhole form a contiguous wildlife complex.

questions.stem: Which tiger reserve is associated with the Bengal tiger swimming in saltwater channels and creeks?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Sundarbans tigers are unique for swimming in the saline/brackish tidal creeks of the mangrove delta.

questions.stem: Ranthambore Tiger Reserve is in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Ranthambore is in Sawai Madhopur district; contains the historic Ranthambore Fort within its boundary.

questions.stem: Which Tiger Reserve in Assam is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to the one-horned rhinoceros?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Kaziranga (UNESCO WHS) hosts the world's largest concentration of one-horned rhinos and is also a tiger reserve.

questions.stem: Melghat Tiger Reserve is located in which Indian state?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Melghat is in the Satpura range of Amravati district, Maharashtra; one of the original Project Tiger reserves.

questions.stem: Which tiger reserve in Kerala is also a famous elephant corridor?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Periyar Tiger Reserve (Thekkady) is known for elephants, tigers, and boat safaris on Periyar Lake.

questions.stem: The NTCA (National Tiger Conservation Authority) was established under which Act?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: NTCA was constituted by the Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Act 2006, adding Chapter IV-B to WPA 1972.

questions.stem: As per the tiger census released in 2023, what was the approximate total wild tiger population of India?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: India's 2022 tiger census (released 2023) estimated about 3,167 tigers — ~75% of the world's wild tigers.

questions.stem: Which tiger reserve in Bihar was upgraded from a national park in 2009?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Valmiki Tiger Reserve in West Champaran, Bihar, is the state's only tiger reserve.

questions.stem: Dampa Tiger Reserve is located in which Northeast Indian state?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Dampa Tiger Reserve (1994) is in Mizoram; it borders Bangladesh and Myanmar.

questions.stem: Which is India's newest Tiger Reserve (designated most recently among major ones)?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Dholpur-Karauli Tiger Reserve in Rajasthan was notified in 2023, becoming India's 55th tiger reserve.
